one_month_reasoning: The window contains Intel's Q3 2026 report on Oct 22 (after close) [22]. Guidance was revenue $15.8-16.8B, 42.0% non-GAAP GM, $0.38 EPS [1]; Intel beat Q2 consensus by ~$1.7B revenue and nearly 2x on EPS [2,3]. Supply-chain checks lean positive for the print: server CPU list prices up 10-15%, Xeon lead times 8-22 weeks and x86 server units +20% y/y [4,9,10]; TSMC and AMD both flagged agentic-AI CPU demand [12,13]. Offsets: PC units weak and memory costs rising 10-15% q/q in 4Q26, which could weigh on the Q4 client guide [6,8], AMD keeps taking share [4], and the stock just fell from $123 to ~$114 in a broad chip selloff on 2007-high 10-year yields [21]. A 14A customer announcement could land in the window but timing is unknowable. Net: close to symmetric around $120, median a touch above spot (~$120.5) for the positive industry read-through, with sigma ~19% for the month (slightly below the 22% implied by 76%/3.5 because realized vol was inflated by deal-headline jumps earlier in the year, but kept wide for the earnings gap).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) P/E: estimated 2028 EPS $2.80 x 36x = $101, and (b) SOTP: Intel Products 2027E NOPAT ~$19B x 20x = $380B + Foundry option value $200B + Mobileye/Altera stakes $9.4B + ~$2B net cash, over ~5.43B diluted shares = $109. Blend ~$105, below the $120 price.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 op income annualized ~$19.3B, +12% for 2027 (DCAI growth from server CPU shortage/pricing [4,9] offset by client unit pressure from memory costs [6,8] and AMD share gains [4]) = ~$21.6B, taxed ~12% (11% guided non-GAAP tax rate [1]) = ~$19B.
Substack framework uses 17x bear / 22-25x base for Products [2]; I use 20x given continued x86 share loss to AMD and Arm (13.6% server share) [4].

Substack base assigns $265-300B [2]; I haircut because external revenue is only $293M/qtr vs a $2.1B quarterly loss [2,3] and the Apple agreement is preliminary [14,15]; credit for Microsoft Maia 2 on 18A [16], 14A conviction comments [17] and reported customer pipeline (social, unverified) [19].
~$52B pro forma cash after Aug $20B offering vs $50.5B debt [2]

bear.story: 14A customer decisions slip or go to TSMC/Samsung, Apple deal stays small/preliminary; memory-driven PC unit decline extends into 2027 [6,8] while AMD crosses 40% server units [4]; market re-rates Intel as a ~17x products company plus a cash-burning fab (substack bear ~$70 [2]).

base.story: Server CPU shortage persists through 2027 with pricing power [9,10], 18A yields normalize [18], EPS tracks ~$2+ for 2027, one or two 14A commitments announced but foundry still loss-making; multiple compresses as EPS grows, leaving the stock roughly flat.

bull.story: Apple M-series on 18A-P ships from mid-2027 and Apple/Nvidia/Microsoft sign 14A capacity reservations [14,16,17,19]; agentic-AI CPU TAM doubling [9,12] lets DCAI grow 40%+ despite share loss; market values foundry as a credible TSMC second source.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$70 (-42%) the market would be pricing near-zero foundry option value and a sub-17x products multiple (substack bear $70 [2]); at that level the likeliest explanation is a fundamental failure (14A customers walk, 18A yield problems, or server share loss accelerating) rather than ordinary 60-75% vol noise.

reasoning: Lane view: the value chain is sending mixed but net-supportive signals. Positives: x86 server units +20% y/y with distributors reporting Intel list-price hikes of 10-15% and 8-22 week Xeon lead times [4,9,10,11]; AMD (EPYC +70%, 2027 server CPU +70% guide) and TSMC (CEO: agentic AI bringing CPUs back) confirm a structural CPU demand step-up [12,13]; Apple (preliminary), Microsoft Maia 2 and other foundry engagements give the foundry real optionality [14,15,16,17]. Negatives: Intel is losing share everywhere (server 65.5% units, ~54% Xeon SP vs EPYC; Arm 13.6% of servers) [4,5]; IDC/Gartner see 2026 PC units -10-11% with memory shortage through 2027, and TrendForce sees PC DRAM supply falling further in 2027 [6,7,8]; foundry external revenue is just $293M/qtr vs $2.1B quarterly losses [2]. Valuation: P/E ($101) and SOTP ($109) give ~$105 fair value vs $120 price at 63x forward EPS [3]; sell-side consensus target ~$108-116 is also below spot [2,3]. Distribution: lognormal-like with median ~$115 (slightly below spot: fair value below price, offset by positive momentum and foundry catalysts) and sigma ~0.58 (below the 76% realized because headline-driven jumps should fade, but far above the large-cap base rate of 25-35%). Scenario mix bear $65/25%, base $115/45%, bull $185/30% gives a mean ~$124, consistent with a right-skewed ladder.
